newsitem.title: GERMANY: Nestle says 1996 German sales rose 2.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Nestle says 1996 German sales rose 2.5 pct.

text.p: Nestle SA managed to increase its sales slightly in Germany in 1996 as new product sales offset declines in other areas such as coffee, the chief executive of its German business said late on Tuesday.

Hans Gueldenberg, chief executive of the group which comprises Nestle Deutschland AG and Blaue Quelle Mineral und Heilbrunnen AG, told a news conference he was also confident for business in Germany in 1997.

Despite weak consumer conditions, Nestle's German sales rose to 7.4 billion marks ($4.6 billion) in 1996, with sales of new products at around 260 million marks although lower coffeee prices cut beverage sales to 1.12 billion marks from 1.16 billion.
